The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

It was good to get a win. We worked very hard for it. It’s so hard to get wins, especially on the road. And now we’re back at home and we have to work on those attributes [that earned us the win] at Forest. We rotated pretty well, there are different aspects of the game we want to improve on regardless of shape.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1299. 'Moments aren't enough': Inside Ethan Nwaneri's struggles on loan at Borussia Dortmund ahead of his return to the Emirates tonight - as Arsenal face dilemma over talented youngster suffering crisis of confidence

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ says Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’

'He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play,' says Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

#1297. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the plan and being patient.”

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1296. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

“We had moments in the game in the first half … [when] we arrived in very dangerous positions,” Arteta said. “With a lot of advantage, our technical quality wasn’t good enough to deliver moments of real threat and especially to be able to sustain the attack, so we allowed certain transitions.” He said that he made some changes at half-time, as managers are wont to do, and that things improved but the real change was clear when he made the substitutions.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta said. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Three different players and a lot of players participating in those goals, so overall very, very happy.” He had played Myles Lewis-Skelly at left-back again to give Riccardo Calafiori a rest. The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Four of those goals came in effective dead rubbers against PSV in the 2025 last-16 (after Arsenal won 7-1 in Eindhoven) and against Kairat Almaty in the final game of last season’s league phase.

So in home Champions League games that matter, they have conceded just four goals in 18 matches: Serge Gnarby and Harry Kane for Bayern in the 2024 quarter-final, Ousmane Dembele in the 2025 semi-final and Lennart Karl for Bayern in last season’s league phase.

Just like against Leeds at the weekend, Arsenal’s closing half hour was their best spell of the match. Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1295. Meet the world's most famous pub team: How a Sex Pistol, Superman and Vinnie Jones took Hollywood United  beyond Sunset Boulevard via private jet - and even rubbed shoulders with David Beckham's LA Galaxy

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

England manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

He later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

This feels a big moment for Carrick and United’s players to answer some of their critics. They have been getting battered from all sides in the last couple of days. Nicky Butt suggested on his podcast that Carrick told him before he got the United job that management “not for me” and “my head’s all over the shop” and that United was the only job he would take. At the very least, those comments are unhelpful and they are thought to have been dimly received internally.

Jamie Carragher offered a lacerating analysis of United’s performance against Spurs on Saturday on Sky Sports on Monday night and suggested things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved if there is not marked improvement. Steven Gerrard questioned why United opted to invest £50m of their summer budget in Andrey Santos, an unused substitute in the last three league games, insisted the back four was not good enough and questioned the work ethic.

And it was interesting to see Carrick alongside his mate Wayne Rooney just now pitchside. Rooney told the Stick to United podcast that captain Bruno Fernandes looks “fed up” and ready to explode at any moment.

It would have been pretty unthinkable for Carrick not to run with a three-man midfield here, not just because of the wide open spaces opponents have exploited this season but when you look at the back line United are fielding. Dalot at left back, two youngsters in Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven and a horribly out of form Lisandro Maríinez.

Nor has Senne Lammens looked convincing this term. Matheus Cunha has been dropped – not before time – and I expect to see Fernandes playing off the right. There’s going to a big onus on Rashford on the left. I’m not sure if he is fully fit but he’s going to be important.

It’s fantastic. It’s where we want to be, these games, these competitions. It’s as tough a place as you can come to. They’ve got a really good history in this competition and it’s where we want to come to challenge and test ourselves. We have put ourselves in this position, got a good start at home and now this is our first away game.

We want a reaction, of course. A positive reaction [to Saturday’s poor performance]. It hasn’t gone how we wanted, how we expected so far but it’s been fine margins in some of those games. It can go both ways but the reality is where we are at now.

It’s a fresh night and we’ve got to adapt, we’ve got to adjust in a positive way.

We want a little more control in the game [with three central midfielders]. At times we have been too open. We wanted to make a difference in that way. We’ve made other changes, certain spaces, certain positions.

To be honest it’s not really a big change of shape, personnel maybe but a lot of it is similar. We want more control, a little bit without the ball and a lot more with it. We’re happy with the way we set up.

Look at the last three goals we’ve conceded. They’re a mixed bag, simple goals you can something about. We need to defend better as a whole team .

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

#1293. Please, Oliver, can we have some more? Celtic boss Martin O'Neill tells Danish midfielder Sorensen it's time to up his game

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

The Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a big reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ said the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as quickly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season

‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I said after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica

‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always said, and that’s been really disappointing.’

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal

Delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

‘He will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

‘Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it. He competes better in the air than I ever thought he could. It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that.

‘He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.’

#1291. Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Araujo rises to score his first goal for Liverpool 🔴 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/W1C4iYd89m

Bradley Barcola gets off the mark for Liverpool with an instinctive finish 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/5K7YBB7UyG

He put his fingers in his ears as he celebrated, with every outfield player running to engulf him, and it was clear how much Barcola was aware of the requirement to get up and running, especially with Cody Gakpo, Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai injured.

Liverpool needed Barcola to deliver as much as the player himself needed to prove a little point and there is absolutely nothing wrong with having a cause to light a fire. Like a batsman who has been waiting nervously to get off the mark, soon the France international began playing his shots.

There were cushioned touches, changes of gear and even a stunned pass to Ryan Gravenberch, using his heel, that showed confidence had started surging through him and how obvious that was when Wirtz sent him scampering away in the 37th minute to finish with his left foot.

Partnership building... 👀 Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola link up for Liverpool's third 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UJC9VW82Q8

That effectively ended the game as a contest, so it was bizarre how it ended up 6-3. Jeremie Frimpong had made it 4-0 and Robert Ljubicic’s reply in the 65th minute looked nothing more than a consolation before Barcola completed his hat-trick.

A brilliant night should have been glossed by Koumas’s first European goal – he matched Steven Gerrard in becoming just the second player aged 21 and under to assist and score for Liverpool in a Champions League game – but LASK kept pushing and exploited spaces to halve the deficit with a double from Florian Flecker, much to Alisson Becker’s obvious disgust.

Look how much it means to Lewis Koumas to score Liverpool's sixth of the night 🥹 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fLYhslbFGq

But some lapses of concentration won’t detract from this being Barcola’s night. The ambition, however, must now be to do it in the Premier League. Liverpool have invested all that money for him to do it over and over again and it would be quite the thing to repeat the trick at Brentford.

“You never know how he is going to play the next day,” Iraola said. “But it wasn’t a big surprise because we were feeling he was in a good place going into the game. He has to enjoy this.”

21 - Lewis Koumas is the second player aged 21 or younger to both score and assist a goal in a UEFA Champions League match for Liverpool, after Steven Gerrard against Dynamo Kyiv in October 2001 (also 21). Emulating. https://t.co/vmfSEaotQ9

A very entertaining way for Liverpool to make it six points from six in the Champions League. The hardest game they have left is Inter away – a fixture they won last season when badly out of form – so they have a real chance to push for a top-two finish that would mean home second legs in the knockout-stages.

This was a good night for Iraola, who was able to rotate before a tough game at Brentford. A hat-trick for Barcola and a much-improved performance from Wirtz were most welcome, but now they need to show some consistency.

Mac Allister and Gravenberch make hard work of clearing a low LASK cross, but they eventually do so. The home team have finished with a flourish and the scoreline looks more respectable for them.

Liverpool’s substitutes have not had the desired effect. Munoz is now on for Barcola, and Ngumoha has gone down with some cramp. The young wingers is substituted, as well as Nyoni, replaced by Mac Allister and Chambers.

Ngumoha too quick for LASK to handle once again, and he is hacked down at the expense of a free-kick. From there, Liverpool win a corner, which they take short and keep possession. Just trying to restore some order in the game.

The score is now LASK 3 Liverpool 6 if you are struggling to keep score. Liverpool have conceded three since Van Dijk was introduced. This was a very tidy finish from Flecker, guiding a bouncing ball beyond Alisson with the inside of his foot.

With the exception of fixtures against a select band of eight or 10 teams, these Champions League nights are becoming like League Cup ties for the Premier League teams: loads of goals, youngsters impressing and senior players in second gear.

The player who scored against Liverpool in December 2023 in the Europa League has done it again, finding an empty net with a diving header after some more loose Liverpool defending.

Denied twice by the offisde flag, Koumas has now scored his first Champions League goal. LASK were caught in possession in their left-back area, and Frimpong delivered to the unmarked Koumas who swept the ball beneath the goalkeeper Jungwirth.

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1290. Freddie Potts on the pain of leaving West Ham, why he had to move on this summer, upsetting the odds in the Champions League with Club Brugge - and why they don't fear Liverpool!

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts says. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’

He is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he says. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday

Potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

#1288. Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

#1286. Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

McGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Emery can make up his mind.

Zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

#1285. Alejandro Garnacho's nightmare Aston Villa loan continues: Struggling star is left at home as Unai Emery picks TWO goalkeepers on bench for Galatasaray defeat before sending warning to ex-Man United winger

Published: 17:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 24 November 2026

Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa was plunged into further doubt on Tuesday as he was overlooked for their defeat at Galatasaray.

The Argentine joined on loan from Chelsea last summer with a £43million obligation to buy, triggered when certain targets were hit.

Yet Garnacho has yet to start for Villa and was not even on the bench in Istanbul, even though two goalkeepers were named.

Asked whether Garnacho was fit for this match, Villa boss Unai Emery said: 'Today I think the best players to play with us, to be with us, were here.'

Daily Mail Sport has reported regularly this season that Garnacho may not see out his loan spell and now that looks increasingly likely to be the case.

There is not thought to be a break clause in the loan but if Chelsea and Villa agreed to cancel it, that would allow Garnacho to go elsewhere in January.

Alejandro Garnacho was not in the Aston Villa squad for their defeat at Galatasaray on Tuesday

Villa boss Unai Emery chose to include two goalkeepers on his bench instead of picking of him

Villa had a similar situation with Harvey Elliott. The midfielder joined on loan from Liverpool in summer 2025 but barely played.

Emery decided quickly that he did not want to sign Elliott permanently and could not risk triggering the appearance clause that would have seen him join Villa for £35m.

Villa are now without a win in six and Emery admitted: 'The next challenge against PSG at home will be huge. If we can recover the three points we lost today maybe we still have a chance to reach the top eight but we are not favourites.'

Emery also bemoaned the home side's time-wasting tactics after Deniz Gul headed them into a 77th-minute lead.

He said: 'I am not blaming the referee but he was unfair with us by adding only five minutes. After they scored it was impossible to play.'
