#1225. Milan injury list rises to nine as Bartesaghi pulls up in training before Olympiacos

Davide Bartesaghi is the latest Milan player to report an injury concern ahead of the team’s Europa League match away against Olympiacos on Thursday and will not travel with the Rossoneri squad for Athens according to the latest updates.

Reports on Wednesday morning confirmed that Francesco Camarda was a strong doubt for the Olympiacos match after suffering an ankle issue earlier in the week.

Now according to reports from Gianluca Di Marzio, Bartesaghi has also pulled up with peritendinitis in his right leg during Wednesday morning’s training session and will not be able to play on Thursday.

Bartesaghi started for Milan in their first game back after the recent international break over the weekend, which ended in a 5-1 victory at home against Frosinone in Serie A.

Milan now have a list of nine players who will not be able to feature in Athens on Thursday night: Bartesaghi and Camarda add to an injury list that already included Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Pietro Terracciano.

It will be a tough test for the Rossoneri on Thursday night, up against an Olympiacos side that sit among the top eight after winning three of their first four matches in the Europa League. Ruben Amorim’s side, meanwhile, have one just once and lost three of their first four matches in the competition.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens went from hero to zero in a matter of minutes during a chaotic first half against Sporting CP in the UEFA Champions League.

With the match ongoing and approaching half-time in Lisbon, Sporting currently leading 1–0, Mauricio Pochettino’s side endured an extraordinary four-minute spell of self-inflicted madness.

The drama began in the 29th minute when Sporting winger Geny Catamo controlled a crossfield pass on the right side of the penalty area, shifted the ball onto his left foot, and drew a clumsy challenge from Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez.

Referee awarded a spot-kick, giving Sporting striker Luis Suárez a golden opportunity to break the deadlock.

However, Lammens guessed correctly, diving low to his left to smother Suárez’s weak effort and preserve the scoreline.

Lammens with an insane penalty savepic.twitter.com/Rkq6y58y6V https://t.co/BtansqlCuR

However, barely a minute after Lammens’ heroics, Sporting launched a straightforward long ball over the top of United’s backline.

Racing recklessly off his line in an attempt to sweep up the danger, Lammens was beaten to the ball by Maximiliano Araujo, who knocked it past the Belgian before being completely flattened in the 31st minute.

??| LAMMENS CONCEDES A PENALTY !!!! HE HAS PUT UNITED IN TROUBLE !!! pic.twitter.com/TbRjncRK7Y

— Kalshi FC (@KalshiFC) November 25, 2026

Stepping up once again, Suárez made no mistake on his second attempt, firing cleanly past Lammens to give Sporting a deserved lead.

#1223. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Thirty-one years ago, Patrick Kluivert scored against AC Milan in Europe. If his son Justin’s eighth-minute penalty will not receive the acclaim of Patrick’s winner for Ajax in the 1995 Champions League final, the goal will be etched in Bournemouth’s hearts.

After Evanilson’s header from a corner struck Koni De Winter’s hand, a VAR review led to Bournemouth being awarded a penalty. Kluivert eyed up Mike Maignan, and waited for the goalkeeper to dive before nonchalantly stroking the ball into the unguarded left corner.

Bournemouth lead against AC Milan in a European competition! 🍒 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/1BQt3wKSr9

And so Bournemouth were beating AC Milan, a scenario that would have seemed unfathomable for vast swathes of these two clubs’ existence. Even more extraordinary was how deserved the goal was: both Kluivert and Evanilson had already spurned opportunities, with Milan seeming overwhelmed by Bournemouth’s intensity.

Watching his side lack any coherence in their passing, Ruben Amorim rapidly came to look as ghoulish as in his last days at Old Trafford. Or, indeed, Michael Carrick in Como 24 hours earlier.

Amorim swiftly had cause to become more irate. Just as Milan had threatened to regain a semblance of control, Maignan inexplicably pushed Tyler Adams in the face when Bournemouth had a corner. VAR had no reason to give Maignan a reprieve from his red card, and Bournemouth’s ensuing penalty.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1222. Spalletti: ‘Ekhator will play against Omonoia, Yildiz is doing great’

Luciano Spalletti has confirmed that Jeff Ekhator is set to play for Juventus in their Europa League match against Omonoia on Thursday evening, says that Kenan Yildiz is progressing well in his recovery from injury, but grew frustrated when asked about his striker situation during his pre-match press conference on Wednesday.

Juventus are due to take on Omonoia at the Allianz Stadium at 20.00 GMT on Thursday evening in their fifth match of the Europa League season.

The Bianconeri have started encouragingly in the Europa League with three victories and one draw across their first four matches, which has them in fifth place ahead of this week’s round of fixtures. Omonoia have won two and lost two of their first four games, leaving them in 18th place on six points.

Spalletti’s press conference began with a quick injury update. The Bianconeri are without long-term absentees Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli, and will also remain without Nico Gonzalez or Pierre Kalulu on Thursday night.

“We have got some players back, except for Nico and Kalulu, the others are available. We have to prepare as best we can because training sessions are starting to get busier. That is a positive, though.”

Spalletti then grew frustrated when asked for clarification on his recent comments about wanting a new striker in January.

Speaking after Juventus’s 4-0 win over Venezia in Serie A over the weekend, Spalletti had discussed the characteristics of his current striking options. Neither Randal Kolo Muani nor Nick Woltemade are considered ‘traditional’ no.9s and Ekhator has been impacted by injuries since joining.

There have been suggestions that Juventus could move for a physically imposing centre-forward in January, but Spalletti was not pleased at his comments being labeled a ‘desperate cry’ for intervention in the transfer window.

“Calling it a ‘desperate cry’ were your words, not mine,” Spalletti argued. “How many times have you asked me about Vlahovic? Even after he left. I spoke about the need for certain characteristics, not a certain player.

“I want to try Kolo in a different position. Woltemade has done very well since coming in, but can’t play all the time. I thought I would put Kolo Muani back there [at centre-forward] for the Venezia game. That was not a desperate cry. I never said that I don’t like Woltemade. We also have Ekhator now and we have to see how he’s doing. He’s a promising young player, we’ll let him play a few times and see if we already have those qualities in-house. When Nico returns, he also has the qualities of a no.9.”

Returning to the topic of tomorrow’s game, Spalletti gave his assessment of the visiting Omonoia.

“Omonia is a team that has picked up six points and beat Celta Vigo. They’re third in their league and have a Norwegian coach who knows modern football very well. They’re a team that plays in a 4-2-3-1 but they are willing to sacrifice and go into a five when they defend. They’ve struggled in some matches, but they always create difficulty for their opponents. We will need to play a very serious game to win.

“We have a lot of top quality players and they’re all good. We also need to develop some young players. We’ll play Ekhator tomorrow because we want an extra solution moving forwards. We will make rotations that we trust in. We’re aware of what is at stake.”

Commenting further on Ekhator’s qualities, Spalletti added: “I think he’s a physical striker who attacks the space well. He’s a player who makes bad balls playable. Baldini speaks very highly of him and Baldini is one of my close friends within football. I’m getting to know him a bit better now and I agree with Baldini.

“I expect him to be calm, but he’s a player with good prospects and all great players started out as a talent with good prospects before reaching that level.”

Spalletti also offered an encouraging update on Yildiz, who has not featured since the first game of the Serie A season.

“He’s doing great. This morning, he started a specialised training session and I can’t wait to have him back in games. We have to wait for the right timing. Being without a player of his level creates a void we somehow need to fill. Being able to replace him with Alajbegovic, Boga or Kolo is great, though, but Yildiz is a champion you can’t simply just replace.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1221. Man United FURIOUS with Howard Webb after he backed decision to send off Leny Yoro at Anfield: Club to take fight to Premier League as red card is OVERTURNED after appeal

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

But United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday

‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ said Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a new contact stalled.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’

#1220. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.

#1219. Spalletti angered by reporters: ‘How many times have you asked me about Vlahovic?’

Luciano Spaletti grew frustrated at reporters during a press conference on Wednesday afternoon, growing tired of questions about Juventus’s need for a new centre-forward during the January transfer window: ‘How many times have you asked me about Vlahovic?’.

Spalletti spoke to the media at a pre-match press conference on Wednesday ahead of Juventus’s Europa League match against Omonoia on Thursday night. You can read Spalletti’s press conference in full here.

Spalletti had also spoken to the media after Juve’s 4-0 win over Venezia in Serie A on Sunday, making it clear that “we need a physical striker who knows how to play with his back to goal.”

There has been speculation over Juventus’s striker situation ever since Spalletti took over just over a year ago. Dusan Vlahovic ultimately ended up leaving the club on a free transfer at the end of last season after more than a year of contract ‘will he, won’t he’. ‘

Juventus’s pursuit of Randal Kolo Muani lasted most of the summer, after a full transfer window of unsuccessful negotiations the year prior, and a long list of other names, including the likes of Alexander Sorloth, Gianluca Scamacca, Gustavo Varela and various others have been linked with the Bianconeri since then.

Spalletti was asked again about his need for a new striker on Wednesday.

“Calling it a ‘desperate cry’ were your words, not mine,” Spalletti argued. “How many times have you asked me about Vlahovic? Even after he left. I spoke about the need for certain characteristics, not a certain player.

“I want to try Kolo in a different position. Woltemade has done very well since coming in, but can’t play all the time. I thought I would put Kolo Muani back there [at centre-forward] for the Venezia game. That was not a desperate cry. I never said that I don’t like Woltemade.

“We also have Ekhator now and we have to see how he’s doing. He’s a promising young player, we’ll let him play a few times and see if we already have those qualities in-house. When Nico returns, he also has the qualities of a no.9.”

Chelsea FC was founded in an upstairs room at the Rising Sun pub on the evening of March 10, 1905. The Blues have endured many ups and downs since then, but in the modern era, they have enjoyed considerable wealth, both on and off the pitch.

From billionaires, both Russian and American, to nimble-footed Italians, net-busting Ivorians, and a host of scintillating South Americans, Chelsea has never been far from the headlines.

The club has also benefited from the leadership of a man known as 'the Special One.' Stamford Bridge has witnessed the lifting of the Champions League trophy on two occasions, and the signing of some of the world's biggest football stars.

Among the rich tapestry of Chelsea fan chants, few are as timeless and cherished as "Blue Is the Colour." This iconic anthem has been an integral part of Stamford Bridge's soundscape for decades, uniting Chelsea supporters and igniting their passion for the club. In this article, we'll delve into the lyrics of this iconic chant and explore other key chants that echo across the Shed End each week.

The tune was originally recorded by the British rock band The Couriers, but it was Chelsea fans who adopted it as their own in the early 1970s.

With its catchy tune and lyrics celebrating the club's signature blue colour, the chant quickly became a fan favourite and a defining symbol of Chelsea's identity.

The song gained even more prominence in 1972 when Chelsea FC reached the final of the League Cup. The club recorded a version of the song with the players and staff, which reached number five in the UK charts, making it the first song ever recorded by a football club to achieve such commercial success.

Blue is the colour, football is the game,

We're all together, and winning is our aim.

Fans sing this chant to express their unwavering support for Chelsea, emphasising the pride in the club's blue colours and their commitment to keeping the Chelsea flag flying high in victory and defeat. It's a simple yet powerful way for Chelsea supporters to show their unity and passion, making it one of the enduring and cherished chants in the club's history.

Set to the tune of the famous ‘Lord of the Dance’ hymn, the "Carefree" chant is a favourite among Chelsea supporters. It's a simple yet catchy tune that embodies the laid-back spirit of Chelsea fans.

This is a chant that celebrates the unity among Chelsea supporters. It's a simple but powerful way for fans to express their

This is a chant that emphasises Chelsea's "super" status and the club's ambition to achieve greatness, be it in the Champions League or in the Premier League. It is heard every single week.

This chant is a variation of "Zigger Zagger" that's often used by Chelsea fans to show their support for the team.

This chant celebrates former midfield dynamo N'Golo Kanté, known for his incredible work rate, beloved smile and ability to break up opposition plays.

It’s apparently a prerequisite of all football clubs to have at least one chant that is ridiculously simple and repetitive. But if you’re a newcomer to the ground, it’s comforting to know that you’ll at least be able to get involved when this one gets sung.

"Chelsea, Chelsea Chelsea, Chelsea Chelsea!"

#1217. He Wants to Join: Man Utd 'Hold Talks' With Man City to Sign Ait-Nouri

Manchester United could be ready to raid rivals Manchester City as they look to boost Mauricio Pochettino's squad in 2027, according to a report.

Despite signing three new midfielders at a cost of more than £150m in the summer, following on from a rebuild of their attack the previous summer, the current Man United squad looks nowhere near good enough.

11 matches into the Premier League season and they have one win and lie 19th in the standings, which shows how poor they have been.

Pochettino has been tasked with turning their campaign around and lifting them up the table, but his reign got off to the worst possible start when they were reduced to 10 men eight minutes in away at rivals Liverpool on Sunday, going on to lose 4-0 on Merseyside.

Aside from Casemiro, the current Red Devils' squad is the same as the one that went on a stunning run of form in the first half of 2026 to finish third behind Arsenal and Manchester City in the top flight, qualifying for the Champions League as a result.

Many of those players look a shadow of the ones that achieved that placing, and it has shown with their performances and results so far this term.

The lack of a recognised number nine in the absence of the injured Benjamin Sesko is something they will look to put right in January, with the Times claiming that it is their top priority for the winter window.

Defence is clearly an issue too though, with only Lens conceding more goals than United's 34 this term from teams who make up the top five leagues in Europe.

The defensive rebuild was on the agenda for the summer but it appears as though it will be brought forward, as club chiefs look at signing a centre-back and left-back hybrid, or potentially even one for each position.

GIVEMESPORT senior correspondent Ben Jacobs reported on deadline day in the summer that United had made a late enquiry for Man City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri, although no move materialised.

Now, TEAMtalk claim that the Red Devils have once again reached out to their neighbours about the Algeria international, with a switch to Old Trafford said to hold high appeal for the former Wolves star.

According to the report, Ait-Nouri has been informed that he can leave the Etihad in January if the deal is right, but Jacobs revealed in September that United were unwilling to agree to City's demands for a loan move with an obligation to buy.

It will be interesting to see if they have changed their stance and if they would be open to a straight loan with an option, because that is something that would surely appeal to the Red Devils given there are suggestions that their budget could be limited mid-season.

Ait-Nouri has struggled to force his way into the City XI ever since joining in a deal worth up to £36m from Wolves, but he does have extensive Premier League experience, he has played in the Champions League, and he has the full-back traits that Pochettino likes.

The 25-year-old may count himself unlucky at how limited his minutes have been at the Etihad, especially this season, but he established himself as one of the best in his position during his time at Molineux previously.

While United are being linked with the likes of Antonee Robinson of Fulham and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, with Ben Jacobs naming a £75m star as another 'one to watch', Ait-Nouri is a strong option to finally provide some strong competition for Luke Shaw.

Shaw has once again shown this term that the club cannot afford to rely on his fitness, even if he could be back on the pitch soon after an eight-match absence.

#1216. Pastore previews PSG vs. Roma: ‘Gasperini’s philosophy is clear, like Luis Enrique’

Former Roma and Paris Saint-Germain attacker Javier Pastore has shared his thoughts ahead of the meeting of his two former clubs in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, and has explained what makes the two teams so enjoyable to watch: ‘Gasperini has made his philosophy clear to the players, like Lucho at PSG’.

Roma face another tough test in the Champions League away against the reigning champions, PSG, on Wednesday night. The Giallorossi have four points from their opening four matches in the competition this season after tests away against Fenerbahce and Manchester United and at home against Slovan Bratislava and Real Madrid.

PSG, meanwhile, have had a perfect start and will be looking to make it five wins from five on Wednesday night. Luis Enrique’s side have beaten Slovan Bratislava, Manchester City, Barcelona and Villarreal already this season.

“Both play to impose themselves with great talents in attack,” said Pastore in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport. “They have coaches who work differently, but with the same attacking and counter-attacking principles. PSG will be more confident and have a perfect record, Roma need to pick up points. It will be an exciting game.”

Pastore feels that the coaches might be both sides’ strongest assets.

“Both know how to get into their players’ heads. They are not just good tactically, but also at managing their teams, which is fundamental in modern football. I don’t know Gasperini very well, but he did great things at Atalanta and he’s brought an offensive, selfless style of play to Roma. They take risks and have lots of quality going forwards.

“He’s made his philosophy clear to the players, like Lucho at PSG, where he has changed the game concepts and the players’ mentality, who still follow him after winning two Champions Leagues.”

Pastore pinpointed the players that Roma should be wary of.

“I’ve always liked Doue and Kvaratskhelia, who won’t be involved unfortunately, but also Mendes and Hakimi, the best full-backs in the world. I also like everything about Neves, a very special player who doesn’t always draw attention, but always helps his team in recovery, building from the back, creating space, looking for smart passes and arriving in front of goal. He’s a complete player.”

“For Roma, Dybala is a spectacle, dangerous anywhere. Malen is better than any other striker this year. And there’s also Soule, who brings something different, is technical and dribbles and scores well.”

Alarmingly for Roma, Pastore says that there are no weaknesses in the PSG side.

“I don’t see any, but maybe they will come out while the game is in progress. PSG are a united team built on the consistency of their play both in attack and defence. And Gasperini is following a similar path with Roma, always wanting to score one more than the opponent. You could even see it against Real Madrid, despite the result.”

Still, Malen’s form is encouraging. The Dutchman has scored 16 goals from 15 games across all competitions and netted four goals during Roma’s 5-1 win over Parma on Sunday.

“With Malen in this type of form, pretty much any ball into the box ends with a goal and it’s hard to stop him. Dybala is dangerous in every situation: From free-kicks, from the edge of the area, with an assist or a shot into the top corner. These are the types of players who usually give you something extra in games like this.”

And lastly, when asked if he had to pick a side, Pastore said: “Rome is beautiful with wonderful people, a place I lived for three great years. I’m in Paris more often because I got married there, and my children were born there. But I would take the Italian food anywhere.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1215. ‘I Played With Wayne Rooney at Man Utd  - I Broke Down When the Judge Issued My Sentence’

A former Manchester United ace, who played alongside Wayne Rooney and Paul Scholes to play a role in the 2010/11 Premier League title-winning season, has revealed he broke down when a judge read out his second sentence.

The player in question, a midfielder known for his physicality and a right foot that regularly attempted and scored ambitious long range efforts - inspired by Sir Bobby Charlton's advice to 'keep shooting' - came up through United's Carrington academy.

He played 60 times for the club, before also making a name for himself at the likes of Everton, Sunderland, and Wolves. He only retired in 2022 after also earning 27 caps for his national team, but the autumnal years of his career saw him stand before court twice, in 2015 and again three years later in 2018.

During his first conviction, in 2015, retired Ireland midfielder Darron Gibson was sentenced to a 12-month community order (including 200 hours of unpaid work) and a 20-month driving ban after admitting drink-driving, careless driving, and failing to stop following a collision with three cyclists in Greater Manchester.

But in a recent interview with RTE Listen, he revealed it was his second conviction only three years later that scared him more. Not knowing whether he was going to be sent to prison for driving under the influence, he revealed (watch the full segment below):

"I was sat in a little side room before we go in [to court], and I'd hired one of the best barristers in England. Solicitor's there, and I've said to him, 'Listen, before we go in, what's the chances of me coming out of here?' And he said, 'It's 50/50.' So I've taken my ring off, watch off, chains, wallet, phone. Passed it all over. And, in the middle of the courtroom, I was sitting on my own on a little chair, I felt I was back at school.

"The judge started talking, obviously there's press everywhere, and the first thing he said was, 'we're dropping this from custodial to non-custodial'. Half the courtroom emptied, all the press left. I just remember breaking down as soon as he said that. And luckily, I didn't go to jail, because I really thought I was."

Instead of going behind bars, Gibson, now 39, was sentenced on May 21, 2018, at South Tyneside Magistrates' Court to a two-year community order (with 250 hours of unpaid work and 30 days of rehabilitation activity), a 40-month driving ban, £800 compensation, costs, and an £85 victim surcharge.

District Judge Roger Elsey opted against a custodial sentence after hearing about Gibson's psychological issues and ongoing treatment, as Gibson has spoken openly about anxiety, intrusive thoughts, severe insomnia, and a nine-year dependency on sleeping tablets.

Later on in the same podcast, Gibson opened up about his nine-year addiction to sleeping tablets, revealing how his dependency nearly cost him his life, in an emotional interview alongside his wife, Danielle.

Danielle recalled the moment she feared her husband was dead, admitting: "I just thought: 'At least he's not struggling anymore.'" He was taking as many as 14 sleeping tablets every night by 2021, alongside several more during the day. His addiction began after suffering a cruciate ligament injury while on international duty in 2013, with anxiety and intrusive thoughts leaving him unable to sleep.

"Looking back, who takes five sleeping tablets at 10 in the morning and doesn't go to sleep? It's ridiculous. But it's where I was," he admitted. Despite previous warning signs, including drink-driving convictions and a serious car crash in 2018, Gibson's addiction continued until he suffered a terrifying seizure at home in November 2021.

Reflecting on just how close he came to losing his life, Gibson told the podcast: "Ultimately, if that hadn't have happened, I wouldn't be here now." Danielle agreed that he might not have survived, prompting an emotional response from her husband.

He mentioned two names but gave the nod to one Man United legend.

Now recovered, the couple hope sharing their experience will help others struggling with addiction and highlight the lack of support available within professional football.

Danielle also criticised the football industry's handling of players' mental health, saying: "He's not the only one that was struggling. There were so many lads, whether it be sleeping tablets or mental health or depression or anxiety or booze." She added that players should have had better access to support, insisting the industry had a "duty of care".

#1214. Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 901–914 (2026) Cite this article

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

#1213. Newcastle Plan New Stadium to be England's Third Biggest Ground

The Premier League is arguably the best footballing division in the world. As a result, English football is incredibly well-backed financially, with owners required to spend millions every season just to keep their team competitive.

Money doesn't just go into huge transfer fees and jaw-dropping salary packages, though. No, to be the very best these days, a club must invest in all areas. This has meant many teams have upgraded or even built new stadiums in recent memory.

The likes of Tottenham Hotspur, Brentford, and most recently Everton have cast aside historic grounds to move into shiny new venues over the past few seasons. While Liverpool are among those to boost their capacity with a smart expansion.

Manchester United are set to spend billions as they finally plan to upgrade on Old Trafford, while Leeds United are planning to redevelop Elland Road. Another iconic Premier League stadium could change in the near future too, thanks to their super-rich owners.

As per reports in The Telegraph back in February, Newcastle United were in the formative stages of looking to complete a major regeneration project as part of plans to build a new £1billion stadium in the city. Interestingly enough, they may still move away from St James’ Park, although that hasn't quite been decided yet, nine months on.

The Toon have already revealed stunning plans for a new £190 million training ground on the 260-acre Woolsington Hall estate near Newcastle International Airport, which they hope to be in by 2029.

It's explained that club officials believe that they can propel the Magpies to the next level by upgrading their current venue, taking the club's value to the £5 billion mark. Revenue certainly would be boosted as a possible new stadium capacity could be as high as 68,000 if moved to Leazes Park – a spot located directly next to St James’ Park.

Financing is also a consideration, and PIF - the current 85 per cent shareholders of the Geordie side - are looking to sell 25 per cent of that to external investors to help fund the project.

Despite pulling the plug on funding for LIV Golf this year, it is understood that the PIF is not losing any interest in the Mags. Instead, they are seeking a minority investor to raise money to fund major projects in the North East. PIF, who jointly purchased Newcastle from Mike Ashley for £305m in 2021, still retain a long-term commitment to the Magpies.

Just five Premier League stadiums make the list.

A final design is yet to be drawn up, but it is expected that construction will take around three years. The cost of a new ground won't be cheap, though, and could exceed £1.3 billion.

It appears as though, despite their wealthy owners, Newcastle will look to the government to help fund the project, with conversations already held about securing public money. As part of their pitch, it's felt that the infrastructure project would modernise the city centre, while The Sun has reported in November 2026 that they are now looking for a minority investor to help speed up the process further.

Indeed, the Magpies have pledged to contribute a large chunk of the financing needed for a wider city regeneration. There is optimism that public money will also be put forward to boost the plans.

Biggest Football Stadiums in England (*subject to renovation plans)

*If renovations are completed as touted **Newcastle United's current stadium size

As things stand, St James' Park is the eighth biggest stadium in England. It would be overtaken by Elland Road if Leeds United's home gets the expansion that has been touted by its owners.

However, Newcastle can then jump up to third on the list, and become the second biggest in the Premier League, if they do indeed complete these proposed new renovations. Only Wembley and Old Trafford would hold a greater capacity in England, while the Principality Stadium in Cardiff (73,931) would also sit ahead of Newcastle, with all UK football stadiums taken into account.

#1212. Guardiola explains to Romario why he should be patient with Ancelotti

Pep Guardiola defended Carlo Ancelotti during an interview with Brazil legend Romario, explaining to his former Barcelona teammate why he should be patient with the Italian tactician: ‘How many World Cups has Brazil played?’

Romario has been one of Ancelotti’s harshest critics, especially after the Seleçao’s elimination from the 2026 World Cup Round of 16.

Guardiola has faced Ancelotti’s teams many times and clearly doesn’t share his former Barcelona teammate’s view.

“How many World Cups has Brazil played? Million! You’ve lost more than you’ve won,” Guardiola said.

Romario argued that he’s not annoyed that Brazil don’t win, but by the way they play.

“I’ve coached Brazilian players, and everyone says the pressure here is greater than anywhere else. It’s very hard,” Guardiola replied.

“I know Carlo a bit. I’ve played against him many times; he’s beaten me a million times. He’s an extraordinary person, and I have no doubt about his ability. He’s come to a new country, to a new culture, and sometimes you need a bit more time. You know there isn’t enough time to train a national team. We’ll see what happens.

“[It happens to] most of the coaches who go from a club to a national team for the first time. I believe that, in the end, football is football; you have less time and have to adapt, but I’m sorry, Mario, I couldn’t doubt Carlo’s ability; it’s impossible, impossible. I know him. People say, ‘He’s good at managing the group’; everyone says he’s the best. I faced him, and he’s very smart. He makes tactical decisions. He knows, as I do, that if you don’t win, you won’t last. Why did I stay at Manchester City for so many years? Because we won a lot. If not, you go home.”

Romario and Guardiola also spoke about their defeat in the 1994 Champions League Final against Fabio Capello’s Milan.

Romario asked Pep whether that Milan side were technically stronger than their Barcelona, but Pep seemed unsure.

“They were very strong, very, very strong. We were too, but they were really strong,” he said.

“It’s very hard with Italian football. Capello had his way of playing, different from Johan’s [Cruijff], but they were a top side.”

In the same interview, Guardiola spoke for the first time about rejecting an offer to coach Italy’s national team last summer, saying he needed to rest and admitting he could have accepted the proposal if it had come at a different time in his life.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1211. Enzo Maresca is still searching for answers after Man City's draw with Napoli: There were glimpses of improvement but individual mistakes again proved their undoing, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 17:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:02 EST, 25 November 2026

The message from Enzo Maresca ought to be clear when Manchester City convene for their meeting at the training ground this weekend before heading down to London. Clear because there is no other appropriate message to impart, really.

He has to say that Arsenal away must be considered the perfect game for his players at this point. The opportunity to reignite their season, to stand up, to show the Premier League they are not going anywhere just quite yet. Squads who went before them would certainly approach a fixture of this magnitude with that attitude. A squad with Kevin De Bruyne as its linchpin would.

City were still searching for answers against Napoli, a point rescued late on by Rayan Cherki. But despite the growing frustration in the stands, that unmistakable guttural desperation for just a bit more of something, it was better. More joined up thinking, at least.

An inverted full back did that for them and it perhaps should be the blueprint for the manager when they arrive at the Emirates on Sunday. City were eminently more comfortable with that; knew where they stood. Nico O'Reilly was not particularly brilliant in that position yet his presence, the safety net of somebody alongside Ayyoub Bouaddi in possession and in turn freeing up Elliot Anderson will surely make City more formidable as the weeks go by.

The set-up presented another tactical tweak for Maresca as he searches for answers and consistency. Defensively, City were twice undone by individual mistakes rather than the overarching plan, one that stifled the enduring class of De Bruyne.

A gentle hum, the half-hearted chants for a returning king, resembled an afternoon session in front of a crowd drowsy from their liquid lunches before a seesawing four-goal second half felt more befitting of City's guest for the evening, UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin – intriguingly entertained by chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in the directors' box.

Rayan Cherki rescued a point late on but this was another difficult night for Man City

Former Man United striker Rasmus Hojlund celebrates his goal against his old rivals

Ayyoub Bouaddi scored his first goal for Manchester City since joining from Lille

City, sporting a fourth kit that had an unfortunate Guantanamo quality to it, certainly had more of a clue than they did here on Saturday. There were clearer patterns – noticeably Marc Guehi piercing midfield lines with one incisive pass for O'Reilly – but this is a team whose confidence has been shaken in recent weeks and that will not return overnight. 'We were aggressive off the ball,' said Maresca, while bemoaning conceding for a tenth consecutive match. 'Defensively we were good, pressing good.'

Regardless, City's supporters definitely demanded more caution thrown to the wind and some of their players wore those looks too. Anderson's dangerous crosses from that right-hand channel – the area presided over by De Bruyne for a decade – occasionally proved unsettling for Napoli, while Allan should have scored from a ricocheting corner as captain Erling Haaland claimed a penalty for being dragged down.

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Guehi 5, Gvardiol 6, O'Reilly 5; Bouaddi 7, Anderson 6; Cherki 7, Fernandez 6 (Ndiaye 63, 6), Allan 5 (Doku 54, 7); Haaland 5.

Napoli (4-1-4-1): Milinkovic-Savic 6; Spinazzola 7, Beukema 6, Rrahmani 7, Olivera 6; Gilmour 8; Politano 6, McTominay 6, De Bruyne 6, Lang 7; Hojlund 7.

In a sign that Maresca was placing more players in threatening areas, O'Reilly had headed over a Matheus Nunes cross – yet chances had been at a premium, those who should be protagonists taking too many safe options rather than pushing chests out and relishing responsibility.

And when there was risk, Napoli pounced. Cherki the culprit, flicking a ball around the corner aimlessly into the middle of his own half. Billy Gilmour gave thanks, punched towards Rasmus Hojlund and he spun Guehi to flash under Donnarumma ten minutes into the second half. Hojlund celebrated by shouting 'one club in Manchester' while holding a single finger aloft. 'It's good banter,' he said and we'll take his word for that.

City had been warned of the danger, when Noa Lang went clean through before checking back upon realising he didn't possess the acceleration to complete the job.

Maresca's assistant, Danny Walker, shook his head on the bench as they pored over the goal's replay. Enzo Fernandez was planting his boot into one of Vanja Milinkovic-Savic's posts when the goalkeeper nonchalantly plucked a floated cross from the night sky.

City had stirred somewhat though, helped by the inclusion of Jeremy Doku – ironically introduced seconds before Hojlund's opener – and it was the Belgian who made their equaliser seven minutes after the hour. He waited and waited inside Napoli's box for defenders to commit, finding Bouaddi alone and the teenager wrapped his left foot around the pass and was quickly racing back to halfway.

There had appeared a head of steam, only for O'Reilly to be caught well out of position as Napoli countered – City carved open – and Lang thundered a volley past Donnarumma with 14 minutes left. Cherki made amends for his earlier error by hammering into the far corner but was less than pleased.

'We played good but we don't give a lot of energy,' Cherki said. 'We need to do more, we need to win these games, and today I don't care (about) scoring my goal. I want to win this game. We're going to London to win.'

#1210. Joe Willock is Exposing Newcastle United Recruitment problem on a weekly basis

Newcastle United still have issues to address in their attack, and it is being exposed by experienced winger Joe Willock, who remains a starter after all these years. Willock came into this season with uncertainty surrounding his future, entering the final year of his contract and with Sean Steur arriving.

Willock found his name in the transfer pages over the summer, but he stuck around, even after Eddie Howe departed, and it proved to be a good decision. The attacker has already racked up 14 appearances across all competitions and remains a starter under Matthias Jaissle.

Willock started in the attacking midfield role in the draw with Arsenal over the weekend, and he has played a key role in the Magpies' recent revival. Willock has two goals and an assist so far this season, and with eight starts in 11 Premier League appearances, he remains practically undroppable as far as Jaissle is concerned.

Still, the 27-year-old is out of contract in the summer, and while there were some reports of potential talks, it doesn't seem as though an agreement is forthcoming.

Some fans have criticised Willock, and there is a perception that the Magpies should be aiming for better, given their ambitions and the money the club has spent over the years. But the midfielder just keeps finding his way into the starting XI, and that says a lot about his character and work ethic. He has even managed to dispel talk that he was simply a Howe favourite, with Jaissle taking a liking to the former Arsenal man in a similar way.

"He is not normal. His energy and the quality he brings to our midfield is something special." - Matthias Jassile on Willock

But it may also say something about the quality of Newcastle's recruitment, and much has been made of the fact no new signings featured in the front four against Arsenal over the weekend. Newcastle are not hitting at the rate they should be with new recruits, and they can't seem to upgrade on Willock who, while very solid, does not have that something special that a club like Newcastle should have in the number 10 position.

The issue is more pressing, of course, because Willock's contract is up at the end of the season. Newcastle are likely to consider a new deal given how regularly he is playing, and Jaissle has said he 'definitely' wants to keep him, but either way, they need to get their act together with their midfield recruitment ahead of the summer. Willock's seemingly never-ending reign over the middle of the mark epitomises that, although that is not to take away from his efforts or talent level, which have been highlighted by more than one manager.

Newcastle United can sign a new centre forward in January with the Magpies interested in the second top scorer in Serie A

#1209. ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

Maresca said: “I’m not worried about Marc at all, he is playing every game since the season started for us and the national team so it’s not easy. He is ok, it [taking him off] was just a technical decision and like in all games managers make changes. He was on a yellow card and sometimes one yellow card can be dangerous.”

When asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca said: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. We will try again to win at Villa next season. I don’t think we deserved to lose but we learn from that and move on. You can always learn something. For sure there are things we can do better today.”

While much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1208. Neto: ‘Excited’ to play for Juventus again after almost ten years

Brazilian goalkeeper Neto will start for Juventus in a Europa League game against Omonia FC tomorrow: ‘I’m really excited to be back on the pitch.’

The experienced goalkeeper returned to Turin on a free transfer in September, replacing the injured Kamil Grabara.

The Poland international suffered a season-ending knee injury, urging Juventus to sign a replacement.

Neto has not played a competitive match since May 30 with Botafogo, and last played for Juventus nearly ten years ago, in May 2017, helping them beat Lazio 2-0 in a Coppa Italia Final.

“It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team,” Neto said at a press conference today, as quoted by Ilbianconero.com.

“Football and life go through different cycles, and there are different people involved. I see a very healthy environment for achieving our goals, and that’s what we need to maintain: the belief that we’re on the right track.

“I was at a point where I was looking for certain things, and whatever I did in the next stage of my life had to make sense,” he added when asked about his return to Juventus.

“I was looking for something that would inspire me. When this opportunity came along, I felt that. It had a different meaning. Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open.

“I’m very happy and satisfied. I enjoy my work, and whatever comes in the future is in God’s hands. I’m here to help, and whatever happens will happen.

“We’re in a place where, wherever you look, you see so many trophies. Whether we talk about it or not, there’s no need to spell it out: we know where we are and what we represent. I’m here to try to achieve great results, and I sense the same ambition around me. Hopefully we can get there. Just like the other teams, we want to win. That’s what we’re fighting for.”

Juventus sit fifth in the Europa League standings with ten points in four matches, but have had very different results in Serie A, where they have already lost three games from 12 and sit 6th in the table, six points behind Milan in four.

Neto, however, has plenty of confidence in his teammates.

“Seeing and feeling the desire these lads have, with so many young players willing to contribute, is truly infectious. From my perspective, that’s a positive thing,” the 37-year-old said.

“There are important players here. We’re talking about Juve. We have the team, the desire and the determination, and hopefully we can get there.

“Every competition is difficult these days. We are Juventus, and whenever Juventus play, we have a responsibility to compete to win. That’s our goal. I haven’t looked at what lies ahead, because at this club you have to fight to win. That’s how it is for me, and I imagine it’s the same for everyone.

“This is a developing team with lots of young players who may be playing in this league for the first time and are still finding their feet. There can be ups and downs. The season is so long that we can’t focus solely on this moment, because in a month we might be talking about something else. My focus is always on giving 100% in training. We need to find balance and consistency.”

Omonia FC have grabbed two wins and two defeats in four Europa League games so far and sit 18th in the table.

“It will be a difficult match. They’re a very strong team,” insisted Neto.

“We’ve watched them, and they counterattack with real quality. I know Fabiano from our time in Brazil. Every game in Europe is difficult, and we know the challenges involved.”

Juventus’ first-choice goalkeeper Vicario will rest tomorrow. He’s on loan from Tottenham, but does he deserve to remain at Juventus long-term?

“I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper,” Neto concluded.

#1207. Why English Clubs Face Being Banned From FIFA Competitions

According to The Independent Football Regulator, a number of big Premier League teams – such as Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool – now face the risk of being banned from FIFA competitions.

While FIFA's main tournament is the World Cup, the football organisation have put an emphasis on the importance of the Club World Cup in recent times. The tournament is now held once every four years and has been expanded to include 32 teams.

The first new edition of the competition took place in the summer of 2025, with English side Chelsea winning the tournament. The Blues netted a cool £84m after beating Paris Saint-Germain in the final, although Auckland City still walked away with £3.3m after finishing 32nd.

With prize money like that on offer, the likes of Man Utd, City, Liverpool, Villa, and Arsenal won't want to turn their nose up at the 2029 Club World Cup – even if it does mean unwanted extra games when players should traditionally be on holiday.

Premier League teams are at risk of being banned from FIFA competitions if they interfere with the English calendar. This is the view of The Independent Football Regulator.

As quoted by The Express, Regulator chair David Kogan told a Digital, Culture, Media and Sport committee:

"There are clearly signs taking place from other entities – and FIFA is the obvious one – where it's creating global club competitions that currently sit outside the normal season of the English game and are held every four years.

"These [competitions] may change. If they change, we will have to look at those very clearly to see what impact they have on the English game and the resilience of the English game. Do we have the powers to then act? Yes, we do."

Kogan then confirmed these powers could be used to keep English teams from taking part in this and similar competitions, depending on the specifics. He warned:

"If another league came and suddenly disrupted the way in which football operates in these five divisions, we'd have to take that very, very seriously."

Traditionally, the English football season runs from August to May. In 2025, the Club World Cup began on June 14 and ran until July 13. When Chelsea and Manchester City took part in the competition – qualifying thanks to their respective Champions League wins in 2021 and 2023 – players had about two weeks from the end of the domestic campaign (25 May), and then another month off before the 2025/26 season started (22 August).

Should the time frame for any future Club World Cups shift, Kogan fears English clubs could be impacted to the point where they can no longer take part in the FIFA competition.

The Argentine winger has been left out of Aston Villa's Champions League squad this week.

With millions of pounds on offer to those who compete, the owners of every Premier League side will be keen to make the 2029 Club World Cup, even if some players might have reservations about the extra game time. As of yet, no English teams have officially qualified for the tournament, with the host nation yet to be announced

As per BBC Sport, a total of twelve European clubs will play in the next edition of the Club World Cup. They can do so by winning the Champions League. PSG have booked their spot after beating Arsenal in the 2025-26 final, and then the 2026-27 and 2027-28 champions will join the French team in the FIFA competition.

They will be joined by the next eight best-ranked teams competing in the Champions League over the next four years. Those are likely to be clubs that reach the latter stages of the competition without winning it. If a team wins the Champions League twice, then the next highest club in the rankings will qualify, and so on.

As such, English sides in the Champions League this season – Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool – all have a shot at making it to the 2029 Club World Cup. However, each European nation is restricted to only two participating clubs.
