(a) Staining and classification strategy. mOSNs in OE sections from Omp-ires-Cre;tdTomatofl/fl mice were identified by imaging tdTomato signal prior to ORCA DNA labelling (left; scale bar: 20 μm). Pcdh DNA loci detected by ORCA (middle) were assigned as mOSN+ or mOSN- based on overlap with tdTomato signal (right). The OE is outlined. Representative images are shown from one experiment. tdTomato-based mOSN classification was performed in three independent ORCA experiments with similar results. (b) Comparison of ORCA contact frequency maps and Hi-C ligation frequency maps for the same genomic bins in mOSNs. (c) Pearson correlation between the ORCA contact frequencies and Hi-C ligation frequencies shown in (b). (d) Pearson r values for the correlation between ORCA contact frequencies and Hi-C ligation frequencies for different ORCA contact thresholds. (e) ORCA contact frequency maps from total OE in two separate wildtype mice. Locus positions corresponding to the Pcdha, Pcdhb, and Pcdhg clusters are labelled. Locus positions containing Pcdh enhancers are labelled with arrowheads. (f) Pearson correlation between contact frequencies from the biological replicates shown in (d). (g) Detection efficiency for each locus position imaged by ORCA from a representative experiment. For (b,d), n denotes the number of individual traces included in the analysis.

(a) Generation of 3D cell segmentations. OE sections were labeled with wheat germ agglutinin (WGA, left; scale bar: 20 μm). Cellpose was used to identify cell boundaries in individual 2D image slices (middle), and these segmentations were linked across Z to generate 3D cell volumes (right). (b) Classification of cell volumes by developmental stage. RNA puncta for marker genes were mapped to the 3D segmentations, and cells were assigned to OSN developmental stages based on marker-expression scores (right); only cells with high-confidence labels were used. (c) Pcdh DNA loci (left) were mapped to the classified 3D cell volumes and inherited the developmental-stage label of their containing cell (right). See Methods for more details.

Example single Pcdh locus traces from horizontal basal cells (HBCs, top) and mature OSNs (mOSNs, bottom), colored by regions that gain H3K9me3 over OSN development. Locus positions gaining H3K9me3 are shown in red and other locus positions are shown in gray. For each trace, the corresponding single-molecule distance map shows pairwise 3D distances between all imaged locus positions. Locus positions corresponding to the Pcdha, Pcdhb, and Pcdhg clusters are labelled below each distance map. Positions that gain H3K9me3 and those that do not are labeled by red and gray bars, respectively. Gray map regions denote missing polymer data.

(a) Cath.a-differentiated (CAD) cells were transfected with plasmids encoding individual Pcdha isoforms fused to mCherry. Cells were then stained with RNA FISH probes targeting different Pcdha isoforms in the probe set. All transfected conditions showed mCherry signal (top panels), but FISH signal was observed only when the FISH probes targeted the same isoform that was expressed (bottom panels). (b) As in (a), but for Pcdhg isoforms. For (a,b), representative images from each transfection/FISH condition are shown. Multiple fields of view were examined for each condition, all with similar results. This validation experiment was performed once. Scale bars: 50 μm.

(a) Example of Pcdh RNA staining for Pcdha6 and Pcdh DNA loci labelled by ORCA in the same cells. Insets show colocalization between Pcdha6 RNAs and Pcdh DNA loci. Images are from a representative field of view from one of two independent experiments with similar results. Scale bar: 10 μm. (b) Schematic of distance measurements used for nascent puncta analysis. For each Pcdh DNA locus, the 3D distance to the nearest RNA punctum was computed. (c) Histograms showing distributions of Pcdh DNA loci by 3D distance to the nearest RNA punctum for three representative Pcdh RNAs. Distances were calculated in 3D voxel coordinate space. Each distribution is bimodal, with a voxel distance of 8 separating proximal and distal populations; puncta within 8 voxel units of a DNA locus were classified as nascent. The threshold at 8 corresponds to a raw distance of 1.2 – 1.6 μm (see Methods for more details). (d) Intensities of RNA puncta within 8 voxels of a DNA locus versus puncta farther than 8 voxels from any locus, for the same Pcdh RNAs as in (c). Significance was assessed using a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Adjusted P values for Pcdha6, Pcdhb16, and Pcdhga1, respectively: P = 1.1 × 10−132, P = 2.7 × 10−58, and P = 7.3 × 10−23. Box plots show medians, interquartile ranges (box limits), notches representing approximate 95% confidence intervals for the median, and whiskers extending to non-outlier extrema within 1.5x the interquartile range. Outliers are not shown.

(a) Example images of Pcdh loci transcribing Pcdh RNAs in H3K9me3-marked nuclear territories. DAPI, H3K9me3 STORM, Pcdha6 or Pcdha11 RNA, and Pcdh DNA are shown for three example cells. Right: individual H3K9me3 STORM localizations and Pcdh traces are shown, with the ORCA barcode corresponding to the transcribed Pcdha gene and detected nascent RNA punctum indicated. Rotated views show the same Pcdh trace and surrounding H3K9me3 STORM signal from multiple angles. DAPI scale bars: 1 μm. Inset scale bars: 250 nm. (b) H3K9me3 nChIP signal over the Pcdha (top) and Tex15 (bottom) genomic neighborhoods in INPs, which highly express Tex15. (c) Tex15 RNA labelling and H3K9me3 signal in an example cell. White arrows denote nascent Tex15 transcription and inferred Tex15 DNA loci. Scale bar: 1 μm. The cells pictured in (a) and (c) are from one combined H3K9me3 STORM, RNA FISH, and ORCA experiment. (d) Distribution of median STORM signal around randomly positioned loci across 1000 simulations compared to the median STORM signal around observed Tex15 sites. The median STORM signal around Pcdh DNA loci from Fig. 2c is also shown. Statistical significance was assessed using a one-sided empirical Monte Carlo test. The P value was calculated as the fraction of simulations with median STORM signal greater than or equal to the observed median. No adjustment for multiple comparisons was applied. (e) Mirrored distributions of local H3K9me3 STORM signal around Pcdh DNA loci and Tex15 nascent sites. STORM signal was measured within the same local radius used in (d) and is plotted as log10(STORM signal + 1). Inset: proportion of Pcdh DNA loci and Tex15 nascent sites with zero detected local H3K9me3 STORM signal.

Transcription probability as a function of enhancer–promoter distance. Points indicate the fraction of promoter observations classified as transcribing within each bin. Data were aggregated across 28 Pcdh enhancer–promoter pairs included in the analysis and 16,399 ORCA traces from mOSNs. Gray bars indicate the number of promoter-to-enhancer measurements per bin. Bin size: 50 nm. Error bars: 95% Wilson binomial confidence intervals around the observed fraction in each bin.

(a) Left: schematic of distance measurements between locus positions and heterochromatin/euchromatin domain centres. For each locus position, dHC − dEC was calculated, where dHC and dEC are distances to the heterochromatin and cluster-specific euchromatin centres, respectively. Negative values indicate greater proximity to the heterochromatin centre; positive values indicate greater proximity to the euchromatin centre. Right: median per-trace dHC − dEC across locus positions in the Pcdhb and Pcdhg clusters for Pcdhb16-transcribing traces with enhancer–promoter contact, Pcdhb16-transcribing traces without enhancer–promoter contact, and non-transcribing Pcdhb16 traces. Vertical dashed lines: Pcdhb16 and its enhancer HS18-22. Red and gray bars: heterochromatic and euchromatic regions, respectively. n: traces per condition. (b) Change in dHC and dEC for Pcdhb16 and HS18-22 in Pcdhb16-transcribing traces with enhancer–promoter contact relative to transcribing traces without enhancer–promoter contact. Schematics illustrate promoter and enhancer positioning relative to the heterochromatin and euchromatin centres in non-contacting (no e–p) and contacting (e–p) states. (c) Median promoter dHC − dEC in transcribing traces without and with enhancer–promoter contact. Each paired set of points represents one Pcdh isoform. For each isoform, dHC − dEC was calculated per trace, then summarized as the median across traces in each contact state. (d) Median enhancer dHC − dEC in transcribing traces without and with enhancer–promoter contact, calculated as in (c). For (c,d), paired points correspond to the same Pcdh isoform or cognate enhancer. Significance was assessed using a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 1.9 × 10−6 and P = 2.6 × 10−5 for (c,d), respectively. 30 Pcdh isoforms were included in the analysis. Arrowheads indicate c-type Pcdh genes or their enhancers. (e) Percent of transcribing traces with and without enhancer–promoter contact for each Pcdh isoform. For all panels, 16,399 ORCA traces from mOSNs were examined; only traces where the relevant promoters and enhancers were detected were included.

(a) Genetic strategy used to generate mouse lines. Black triangles: loxP sites. (b) Immunostaining for RAD21 (top) and SETDB1 (bottom) in heterozygous and homozygous animals. Representative images are shown from one of two independent experiments with similar results. Scale bar: 50 μm. (c) H3K9me3 nChIP-seq over the Pcdh locus in four WT (Omp-GFP) and three Setdb1cKO biological replicates. Data were generated across two independent experiments. The two additional WT replicates in Fig. 5c are shown in Fig. 1h. (d) Top: median distance of each locus position to the heterochromatin (HC) domain centre in Rad21cKO and WT mOSNs. Bottom: Rad21cKO - WT difference. Yellow bars: Pcdh enhancers. (e) Top: mean pairwise entropy for each locus position in Setdb1cKO and WT mOSNs. Entropy was calculated from pairwise distance distributions to all other locus positions and averaged across partners. Bottom: Setdb1cKO - WT difference. For (d,e), shaded regions: 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. (f) Change in percent of mOSNs expressing each Pcdh gene in Rad21cKO (top) and Setdb1cKO (bottom) relative to WT. (g,h) Change in percent of mOSNs expressing Pcdhb and Pcdhg genes relative to WT as a function of distance to cognate enhancers in Rad21cKO (g) and distance to the heterochromatin/euchromatin boundary at the Pcdhb/Pcdhg region in Setdb1cKO (h). (i,j) Percent of mOSNs expressing each Pcdh gene as a function of enhancer–promoter contact frequency in Rad21cKO (i) and Setdb1cKO (j). In (g-j), contact frequency was calculated for each Pcdh promoter and cognate enhancer. Dashed line in (j) indicates a linear fit to heterochromatic Pcdh genes, with Pearson correlation shown. (k) Model of Pcdh transcription from a megabase-scale heterochromatin domain. Pcdh enhancers lie outside the heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh promoters. Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion brings enhancers into the domain to engage promoters, with transcription initiating from within the domain. After promoter activation, transcription can proceed in the absence of enhancer—promoter engagement. Transcription reads through downstream Pcdha and Pcdhg genes residing within the heterochromatin domain, and domain-scale compaction is maintained.

This file contains Supplementary Fig. 1 and Tables 1–5. Supplementary Fig. 1 shows example FACS plots for the isolation of GFP+ and tdTomato+ mOSNs. Supplementary Tables 1–5 list DNA sequences of genotyping primers, quality control and analysis statistics for scRNA-seq data, ORCA experiment details and genomic coordinates of ORCA barcodes.

#1188. Champions League official line-ups: PSG vs. Roma

Roma aim for the stars with Santiago Castro, Matias Soulé and Manu Koné against giants Paris Saint-Germain, as Paulo Dybala, Bryan Cristante and top scorer Donyell Malen are benched.

It kicks off at the Parc des Princes at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Inter vs. Stuttgart on the Champions League liveblog.

It has been a tricky campaign for the Giallorossi so far, as they are pushing for the top of the Serie A table and still unbeaten there, but have highlighted a distinct lack of experience in Europe.

This saw them twice throw away two-goal leads to Real Madrid and Manchester United, leaving them on four points in as many rounds.

The injury crisis is finally calming down, with Mile Svilar and Paulo Dybala making their comebacks at the weekend, where Malen scored four goals in a 5-1 drubbing of Parma.

However, Malen and Dybala do not start in Paris, as Niccolò Pisilli is drafted in to bolster the midfield with Soulé and Koné.

Santiago Castro therefore leads the attack instead, perhaps hoping to tire PSG out before unleashing their biggest talents, seeing as Roma have shown a tendency to fall away.

Marten de Roon is also preferred to Bryan Cristante in the midfield.

Devyne Rensch and Lorenzo Pellegrini are the only remaining absentees.

Paris Saint-Germain won the last two editions of the Champions League, but their chances of a hat-trick have been badly damaged by losing two stars for the rest of the season.

Just weeks after former Napoli hero Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his anterior cruciate ligament, Désiré Doué suffered the same fate.

This is a special fixture for coach Luis Enrique, who started his senior management career at Roma in 2011/12.

There are other familiar faces, as Marquinhos was at Roma in 2012/13, while Fabian Ruiz made his name at Napoli and Achraf Hakimi first shone for Inter.

PSG need to reshuffle with Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos dropped, so Maghnes Alkiouche, Ferran Torres and Senny Mayulu all start together.

PSG: Safonov; Hakimi, Zabarnyi, Willian Pacho, Nuno Mendes; Joao Neves, Vitinha, Fabian Ruiz; Akliouche, Ferran Torres, Mayulu

PSG bench: Chevalier, Bar, Lucas Beraldo, Marquinhos, Dembele, Digne, Lucas Hernandez, Godts, Dro Fernandez, Zaire-Emery, Boly, Ndjantou

Roma: Svilar; Mancini, N’Dicka, Hermoso; Wesley, De Roon, Koné, Molina; Soulé, Pisilli; Castro

Roma bench: De Marzi, Gollini, Koulierakis, Cristante, Malen, Dybala, Balerdi, Lulli, Rodrigo Mora, Ghilardi

#1187. Jude Bellingham scores 'the best goal of my life' as his stunning long-range volley helps Real Madrid come from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and important for the win as well.'

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week

4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week

5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

#1186. Amorim: ‘Milan must do well in Europa League and Serie A, only way to be a good team’

Ruben Amorim warns Olympiacos are ‘aggressive, especially at home’ in the Europa League, but Milan ‘have to do well both in the League and in Europe, it’s the only way to be a good team.’

It kicks off in Athens on Thursday at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).

Injuries are piling up for this trip, with Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi joining Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Fikayo Tomori, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano on the treatment table.

At least Mike Maignan is available again after suspension, and confidence was boosted by a 5-1 Serie A victory over Frosinone.

“It’s a fact that we need to improve in the final third,” said Amorim in his press conference.

“The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that’s the only way I can help my players. Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

“We need to improve, even in our defending. We’ve almost always conceded a goal, so that’s another area we need to improve.”

Olympiacos are sixth in the Europa League table after amassing 10 points from four games, beating Jagiellonia, Olympique Marseille and Sparta Prague before the 0-0 draw away to Stade Rennais.

Notably, they have conceded only one goal in those four matches.

“They’re a strong team. They’re aggressive, especially at home. I’ve played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do. They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3, they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players.

“They’re a strong team, and with their fans there, it’ll be a tough match. Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.”

The Rossoneri’s form in the Europa League has been little short of disastrous, as the 4-0 victory away to RB Salzburg was an outlier between three defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring a single goal.

“To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe,” insisted Amorim.

“That’s the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan. I’m always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn’t take much to change the situation. That’s what I’m trying to make my players understand, because it won’t always be this way. We’re at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone.

“We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at big clubs. We have to be ready for this. I can’t believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated.

“We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We’re building so many things. Tomorrow is another test for us.”

Does Amorim still believe that Milan will be able to challenge for the Scudetto?

“I haven’t changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we’ll do it.”

Many coaches have been asked about the release of the Grand Theft Auto VI game and how much time players are committing to it.

“I’d rather my players play that every day rather than scroll through social media,” replied Amorim.

“Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven’t read anything, because that’s how I want to live my life.”

#1185. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and said: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

These are the only two awards which are a given as they are factual. They are given to the top scorer from the previous season, which on the men’s side in 2025-26 was Harry Kane, who found the back of the net 73 times for club and country. Mexican Charlyn Corral, who plays her club football for Pachuca, wins the women’s award. Former England striker Alan Shearer and British actress Sophie Turner are on hand to give out the awards.

Kane received a big cheer from the crowd. He will be hoping this is not his final award of the night.

So the rumour before the ceremony was that Lamine Yamal would win the young talent, Harry Kane the best striker and Kylian Mbappe the Ballon D’Or. The first two of those predictions have proved to be true. Hopefully the third will not be.

One of those to win the Ballon d’Or multiple times is former Liverpool and England forward Kevin Keegan, who died back in July. Keegan won both of his awards whilst playing his club football at Hamburg and his death means that Michael Owen is currently the only living English winner of the award, although that might be changed soon if Harry Kane wins tonight.

The fans have the chance to vote for their B.O.A.T, ie. their favourite Ballon d’Or of all time. There are 10 nominees for those who have won the award multiple times. Voting for that award finishes tomorrow night and will be announced in a few days.

Patrick Vieira and Sol Campbell have remained on stage and give the award to PSG, who made it back-to-back Champions Leagues last season. Former Arsenal teammates Sol Campbell and Patrick Vieira are welcomed onto the stage to hand out the award for the Women’s Club of the Year. Unsurprisingly, it goes the way of Barcelona, who were imperious over the last year. The president of Barcelona Joan Laporta is the man to come up top receive the award.

Named after Brazilian footballer Socrates, awarded for the best humanitarian work done by a footballer, the award goes to Arsenal and England forward Bukayo Saka and he is given the award by Burna Boy. This award is presented in collaboration with ‘Peace and Sport.’ Saka, as part of his speech, gets out a piece of paper written by a 14-year-old from Rwanda and the young child speaks of his desire to become an English teacher one day.

Another award goes the way of a Spaniard as Spain’s number one between the sticks Unai Simon seals the award after becoming a world champion over the summer. Simon pays tribute to his parents, brother and partner, who he says bring calm in their life.

Really this ceremony should be taking place in Madrid.

The 25-year-old continues Spain’s dominance tonight as she receives the award from Peter Schmeichel. Coll was part of the dominant Barcelona team over the last year. Coll has her parents in the auditorium tonight and pays tribute to them.

Can anyone stop Spanish people right now?

Four of the five nominees are Spaniards and one of them wins it in the form of Luis de la Fuente, who led Spain to World Cup glory over Argentina back in July. He shares an embrace with a few of his players who are in attendance tonight. He apologises for his lack of English and hopes it will be better in the future. Could that indicate that he hopes to manage in the Premier League at some point? He pays tribute to the other nominees, his group of players and technical staff.

The other was Vincent Kompany, who is unable to attend as he is in hospital and they wish him the best.

A lot of support in the auditorium for Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta and also Aston Villa’s Unai Emery, with both being cheered loudly, in the category of men’s coach of the year. But there really could be only one winner and that is rightly Spain’s Luis de la Fuente who added the World Cup this summer to already winning the European Championship.

Former Liverpool manager Rafael Benitez is welcomed out to give the award to Pere Romeu of Barcelona. One Spanish manager giving the award to another. So far, all three awards have gone the way of Spaniards.

England great Lucy Bronze is on hand to give the award to Barcelona’s Vicky Lopez. Two Spaniards and Barcelona players have now picked up the first two awards. Lopez pays tribute in her speech to her mother.

VICKY LOPEZ IS THE 2026 WOMEN'S YOUNG TALENT OF THE YEAR! ✅ 2025 ✅ 2026 Back-to-back winner. #ballondor https://t.co/VvlQZuxA2D

2004 Ballon d’Or winner Andriy Shevchenko is brought onto the stage to hand over the award to Spain and Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal. Is that an indicator that he may not win the main award?

He says it is an honour to win the award and pays tribute to his club and international teammate Pau Cubarsi, who he believes should have won the award. It is the third straight year he has won this award and his younger brother is in tears.

After delivering his speech in Spanish, presenter Thierry Henry then asks an awkward question of whether this is the award he really wanted. Yamal nervously laughed it off but that certainly was an awkward moment.

So Lamine Yamal has won the men’s young talent of the year award. Is that a sign that he will not also win the main prize? He was hotly tipped for this one as a consolation prize. So maybe it really is between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe? Presenter Thierry Henry has asked Yamal - still just 19 - if the award “is the one you really wanted tonight?” The answer is surely no.

45 minutes later than originally schedule, the 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony is officially under way. Instead of getting under way though with some awards, we have a performance from British singer Jorja Smith.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more important than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

There's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before quickly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

#1184. Chivu: ‘Inter must be best version of ourselves’ against VfB Stuttgart

Cristian Chivu wants Inter to be ‘the best version of ourselves’ in the Champions League against VfB Stuttgart this evening, with an update on Lautaro Martinez.

It kicks off at San Siro at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and PSG-Roma on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Nerazzurri’s confidence took a knock on Sunday in Serie A when they fumbled a 4-2 lead for the chaotic 4-4 draw away to Atalanta.

They are also playing catch-up in Europe, having lost the first two matches against Real Madrid and Club Brugge, then got back on track beating Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

“We must be the best version of ourselves,” Chivu told Sky Sport Italia.

“We are well aware of the importance of this match, we are playing at home, and must give a sense of consistency to our recent good performances in the Champions League.”

VfB Stuttgart are one point ahead of Inter in the Champions League table going into tonight’s match, as they won the first two, drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid, and lost 2-0 away to Galatasaray.

Pio Esposito scored a hat-trick against Atalanta at the weekend and Lautaro Martinez made his comeback after more than a month out, but is not risked from the start tonight.

“Lautaro is recovering his fitness and ready to come on in the second half. Marcus Thuram has played practically non-stop in recent months, and we need him again this evening,” explained Chivu.

#1183. Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3,4,5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6,7,8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

a, Detailed schematic of the pulse sequence, showing the various stages of the protocol. b, p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration and pulse ramp time. Parity oscillations remain visible even for slow ramp duration up to approximately 75 ns. An oscillation as a function of ramp duration is also visible at zero pulse duration, indicating that the qubit evolves partially during the ramp of the coupling pulse. c, Time trace and corresponding histogram of the readout signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) with the left chain on resonance and the right-chain QDs off-resonance, using 400 μs readout time. Transitions between \(| e\rangle \) and \(| o\rangle \) are attributed to quasiparticle poisoning. d, Dwell time histogram from c. e, p(e∣e), p(o∣e), p(e∣o), and p(o∣o) while varying the pulse amplitude VC and ramp time. For fast ramps (≲5 ns), parity mixing is observed between the chain and the dot. We attribute this to a diabatic excitation of the coupled system, which rapidly decoheres before the final measurement. In the main text, we use ramp times of 25 ns to avoid these excitations. For pulse amplitudes ≲11.5 mV, no parity mixing is observed, which we use to roughly identify when QDC passes through resonance. f, Schematic of the configuration for the measurements in c-e. g-j, Same as c-f, but for the right chain, with the QDs of the left chain off-resonance. In panel i, parity mixing between the chain and QDC is observed for ramp times  ≲ 10 ns, indicating a slightly weaker coupling between QDC and the right chain versus the left chain.

Readout characterization using time traces of the reflected resonator signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\), measured for three different amounts of detuning with the coupler QD kept fixed far from resonance. Thresholds used for single-shot state identification are obtained by fitting a Gaussian mixture model. The detuning configuration in (e-g) is used for qubit readout. a, Schematic representation of the readout configuration with both chains on resonance. b, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in a. Residual coupling between the chains results in inter-chain hopping that is faster than the readout time of 500 μs, preventing readout in a single shot. The two quantum capacitance signals corresponding to the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) states are partially averaged which makes them difficult to distinguish from the \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) states. c, As in a, but with both chains detuned from resonance. d, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in c. The slight detuning suppresses inter-chain hopping, though it remains too fast for high-fidelity single-shot readout. Two distinctive regions can be observed: When the system is in the global even state, rapid jumps between \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| ee\rangle \) are visible. When the system is poisoned, it enters the global odd manifold. Transitions between \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) are not resolved because they produce similar readout signals. e, As in c but with both chains detuned further from resonance. f, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in e. The two computational states \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) correspond to the red and blue signals, and can now clearly be resolved. The green signal contains both leakage states of the odd global parity manifold (\(| eo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \)). Due to the antisymmetric detuning where the ground state of one dot is full and the other is empty, the \(| oo\rangle \) state is energetically favored over the \(| ee\rangle \) state, resulting in a skewed population between the two. Transitions are mainly observed between the even and odd global manifolds. The signal-to-noise ratios between the leakage distribution and the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) distributions are 2.88 ± 0.28 and 2.76 ± 0.09, respectively. Integrating the fitted Gaussian distributions across the assignment thresholds gives false-leakage probabilities of 0.45% for \(| ee\rangle \) and 0.25% for \(| oo\rangle \), showing that finite readout SNR accounts for only a small fraction of the observed leakage. g, Dwell time histogram of the three observed states, indicating the difference in lifetimes. The shortest measured state lifetime in this readout configuration is 8.3 ms, corresponding to a probability of approximately 5.8% for a state transition during the 500 μs integration window. The trace is acquired with the coupler QD kept far from resonance, showing that state switching on this timescale is already present in the readout configuration. These transitions include both residual inter-chain hopping and quasiparticle-poisoning events and can produce time-averaged signals that are assigned as leakage for pulsed measurements.

Conditional probabilities at the simultaneous sweet spot for the two chains in both the even and odd global parity manifolds, corresponding to Extended Data Fig. 5g but extended to larger pulse amplitudes. Additional outer lines appear when the energy of the detuned chain is aligned with the first excited state of the other chain. The quadrant in which they appear depends on the initial state of the system, as well as the global parity manifold (‘Interpretation of pulsed charge-stability diagrams’ in Methods). a, Left chain in the even manifold. b, Right chain in the even manifold. c, Left chain in the odd manifold. d, Right chain in the odd manifold. The QDR2 resonance is shifted by approximately 3 mV with respect to panel b due to the Coulomb interaction with the additional electron on the parity-switching QD. The odd-manifold measurements include two parity-switch passages, before and after the control sequence. Comparing the background return probabilities in the even- and odd-manifold measurements for initial states \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \) gives single-passage parity-switch fidelity of 99.77 ± 0.03% (‘Parity-switch fidelity’ in Methods).

a, Map of p(oo∣oo) (left) and p(oe∣oe) (right) as a function of the left and right hybrid-gate voltages (VLH and VRH). The diagonal and antidiagonal features of enhanced parity mixing correspond to degeneracies between the qubit basis states. The points labeled c-k indicate the VLH,VRH values used in the remaining panels. b, Schematic representation of the four configurations measured at each point: left- and right-chain pulsed charge-stability diagrams in the global even and odd parity manifolds. c-k, Pulsed charge-stability diagrams measured for the left and right chains in the even (top) and odd (bottom) parity manifolds. Unlike conventional charge-stability diagrams referenced to the Fermi energy in a normal lead, here each chain provides the energy reference for the other. As such, the measured features reflect the difference between the excitation energies of the two individual chains. Crossings are therefore observed simultaneously for the left and right chains when the splittings of the two chains compensate each other, corresponding to the qubit degeneracy condition. Consequently, the appearance of a crossing in a single parity manifold does not imply that the corresponding chain is tuned to its sweet spot. Indeed, crossing-like features are observed in only one manifold in panels c, e, i and k. The orientation of the avoided crossings depends on the parity manifold: in the even manifold, the left and right chains exhibit the same orientation, whereas in the odd manifold the orientation is reversed, reflecting the sign difference ε12 ± ε34 between the two manifolds. Only near the sweet spot (panel g) are crossings observed for both chains in both parity manifolds simultaneously, providing a unique signature that both chains are individually tuned to their sweet spots.

Pulsed charge-stability diagrams showing p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of the right-chain gate voltages (VR1, VR2), for various values of the coupler QD pulse amplitude VC for a fixed pulse duration of 10 ns. The value of VC is indicated above each panel. The device configuration is the same as in Extended Data Fig. 8. a-h, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ 0. As VC is made more negative, the coupler QD is first brought closer to resonance and parity mixing along the degeneracy lines increases. Eventually, when the coupler QD is near or below resonance (around VC = − 9 mV), the final state is dictated by the ground state of the chain in the relevant sector of the charge-stability diagram irrespective of the initial state. We note that the chain appears to move from CAR-like at low pulse amplitudes (tR < ΔR, a) across a sweet spot (tR ≈ ΔR, b-e) to ECT-like at high pulse amplitudes (tR > ΔR, f-h), which we attribute to uncompensated cross-capacitance between VC and VRH. i-n, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ π. The main difference is that the visibility of QDR2 is suppressed, as predicted by theory (Supplementary Note 4).

p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics, corresponding to measurements shown in the main text. Unless stated otherwise, measurements are taken at VC = 9.8 mV and perpendicular field B⊥ = 15.6 mT (yellow mark in panel o), corresponding to a phase difference φ ≈ 0 between the chains. a-d, Detuning individual quantum dots. e,f, Detuning the left- (e) and right-chain QDs (f). g,h, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (g) and inner (h) QDs of both chains. i, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude. j, Varying VLH and VRH for a fixed pulse duration of 18 ns. The colored marks indicate sweep directions for panels k,l,p,q. k,l, Detuning the left (k) and right (l) chain via VLH and VRH. m, Oscillation frequency as a function of pulse amplitude in logarithmic scale, where V0 is the gate voltage at which QDC is on resonance. The gray line fits f = K/(V0 − VC) with K = 156.6 ± 0.3 MHz mV and V0 = 11.285 ± 0.002 mV for VC < 10.8 mV. n, Quality factor of the oscillations as a function of VC. o, Dependence on the out-of-plane magnetic field B⊥. p,q, Symmetric (p) and antisymmetric (q) detuning of VLH together with VRH.

p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics. Note that for this dataset, the chains were tuned using pulsed charge-stability diagrams but were not compared to the odd manifold. As such, it is unclear if the even and odd states of each chain are degenerate. a, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude VC. In contrast to the main text, QDC starts detuned below the Fermi level instead of above but is likewise pulsed closer to resonance for qubit evolution. b, Dependence on the out-of-plane magnetic field B⊥. In this case, we observe decoherence around φ = π (B⊥ ≈ 13.5 mT), consistent with a small residual detuning of an outer QD from resonance; such detuning restores transverse coupling near φ ≈ π (Supplementary Note 4). c,d, Detuning the left (c) and right (d) chain via VLH and VRH. e-h, Single-dot detuning of VL1, VL2, VR1 and VR2. i,j, Detuning the left- (i) and right-chain QDs (j). k,l, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (k) and inner (l) quantum dots of both chains.

p(eo∣eo), p(oe∣oe), p(eo∣oe), and p(oe∣eo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics, corresponding to measurements shown in the main text. a, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude VC. b,c, Detuning the left (b) and right (c) chain via VLH and VRH. d, Varying VLH and VRH for a fixed pulse duration of 18 ns. The colored marks indicate sweep directions for panels b,c,e,f. e,f, Symmetric (e) and antisymmetric (f) detuning of VLH together with VRH. g-i, Oscillation frequency (g), Rabi decay time \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) (h) and quality factor Q (i) extracted from panel a as a function of VC.

Extracted Rabi coherence time \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) for the different detuning configurations shown in Fig. 4, as indicated by the schematics. a-d, Detuning individual quantum dots. e,f, Detuning the left (e) and right (f) Kitaev chains. g,h, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (g) and inner (h) quantum dots of both chains. Gray markers indicate fits for which the relative uncertainty in \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) exceeds 50% or the fitted oscillation frequency lies outside the 10–200 MHz range, and are therefore considered unreliable. For visibility, the \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) axis is also limited to 40 ns. Fitted values beyond this range are not shown, as they also arise from unreliable fits and are not physically meaningful. The same-chain two-dot detunings show the narrowest range over which coherent oscillations can be reliably fitted, whereas the single-dot and cross-chain detunings retain resolvable oscillations over a broader range. The simultaneous two-dot detunings in panels e-h use the same voltage scales as the corresponding single-dot measurements in panels a-d, and the pulse amplitude applied to the second quantum dot is shown on the upper axis.

Supplementary Notes 1–4 describing the numerical simulations with quasistatic noise, the effective low-energy Hamiltonian for imperfect Majorana states, the pulsed charge-stability diagrams, and the consequences of imperfect Majorana states. #1182. Trinity Rodman pulls out of USA roster for upcoming tournament just hours after shock split from Ben Shelton

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER and DAN MATTHEWS

Published: 22:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 07:55 EST, 25 November 2026

United States women's soccer star Trinity Rodman has backed out of an upcoming tournament hours after reports revealed she is no longer in a relationship with tennis star Ben Shelton.

Rodman was set to take part in the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship window in Texas, but has now pulled out due to what US Soccer called 'a minor shoulder injury' in a statement announcing the roster move.

The statement says the injury occurred during the 2026 NWSL Championship Game last Saturday, where Rodman and the Washington Spirit fell 2-1 to the Kansas City Current. US Soccer has replaced Rodman with Gotham FC winger Jaedyn Shaw.

Rodman's removal comes hours after the Daily Mail was first to report on her split from the American tennis star.

The American sporting couple began dating around March 2025, frequently supporting one another at their various events, but have recently decided to call time on their relationship.

Their conflicting work schedules and constant travel made it too challenging for the couple to continue maintaining their relationship, the Daily Mail understands. However, the pair are believed to remain close, despite their split.

American soccer stat Trinity Rodman has backed out of the USWNT roster for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship taking place beginning later this week

The announcement comes hours after the Daily Mail was first to report her split from longtime boyfriend and tennis star Ben Shelton

US Soccer says Rodman suffered 'a minor shoulder injury' in the 2026 NWSL Championship

The couple were frequently forced to maintain their romance over long distance with Shelton constantly traveling around the globe while playing on the ATP Tour.

Despite multiple sacrifices and last-minute trips to attend each other's matches, it appears they could no longer make it work.

The Daily Mail has reached out to both Shelton and Rodman's representatives for comment.

Shelton, 24, suffered defeat in the semi-final of the ATP Finals on Saturday, losing 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7-1) to Carlos Alcaraz in Turin, Italy.

The same evening, Rodman, 24, and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL final to the KC Current.

The following evening, the American tennis star was spotted at Madison Square Garden for the New York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers without Rodman, instead sitting on Celebrity Row alongside a friend and actress Inde Navarette.

The couple first went public with their relationship in March 2025 following speculation from fans.

Mystery surrounded the early stages of their relationship, as they initially dropped a playful hint as part of a TikTok trend last March then 'hard launched' their romance soon afterwards.

Their conflicting work schedules made it too challenging to maintain their relationship

The sporting power couple went public with their relationship around March 2025

Rodman was a near-permanent fixture in Shelton's box throughout the US Open in September.

The USWNT star and the Spirit had played an NWSL game in Washington on the day of the final but Rodman left the capital almost immediately after the final whistle to make the mad dash to New York for Shelton's final.

The forward was captured crying inside Arthur Ashe Stadium in the wake of her boyfriend's loss to Alexander Zverev.

Rodman, the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, had cheered on the World No 4 at multiple other events, making her Wimbledon debut in May 2025.

Meanwhile, the tennis superstar was every bit the supportive boyfriend when he consoled Rodman after her team lost the NWSL championship game last November.

The World No 4 attended the Knicks game on Sunday, one day after losing the ATP semifinal

Rodman and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL Championship to the KC Current on Saturday

The Washington Spirit were stunned by underdogs Gotham FC in California, as footage from the game showed Shelton consoling an emotional Rodman as she burst into tears on the sidelines.

Shelton opened up on the challenges of their relationship in September, admitting that it was tough for the couple to continuously make time for one another.

'It is really difficult,' the Grand Slam finalist told US Weekly. 'I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.'

He added: 'Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I'd say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We're not where we want to be yet, we're not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time.

'This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.'

#1181. Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM

The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

FLEETWOOD TAKE THE LEAD! 😱 Loupalo-Bi puts League Two side Fleetwood ahead against Arsenal 💥 https://t.co/zTFEkCp0oL

As the home fans set off flares, filling the air with plumes of thick, red smoke, the theme tune to Captain Pugwash was played. Arteta tried to find answers from his coaching staff, amid the cacophony, but occasionally you do not have to look too deep for answers.

Could the miracle happen? When half-time arrived with Fleetwood still in the lead, you began to wonder. But then you saw Ben White and Martin Odegaard go through intense warm-ups so they could be introduced at the start of the second half and you knew the mountain had become taller.

So it proved. Odegaard, with his mesmerising left foot and all-encompassing vision, did more in the first five minutes of the second period than many of his colleagues had managed before the interval, and Arsenal levelled in that initial flurry through Gyökeres’s first domestic goal of the campaign.

Viktor Gyökeres gets his first goal of the season and Arsenal are level against Fleetwood! 🔴 https://t.co/LfZcIbAfCX

A game of attack against defence played out for the remainder before Dowman was harshly dismissed in the 85th minute after reacting to a tough challenge from Neal. There was still time for Fleetwood’s Lynch to make two excellent saves from White and Odegaard in added time as Arsenal tried to avoid the shoot-out lottery. They could not and how it hurt them.

HUGE save from Jay Lynch! https://t.co/dLJaFwCmHQ

“Football’s getting a little bit more, I don’t know, clinical and removed,” Matt Lawlor, the Fleetwood manager, said. “To me, there was that feeling we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it? To be a part of it is special.

“To be giving that to football fans and especially Fleetwood fans is unbelievably special. I’m really proud of it. Football’s a funny old game, isn’t it?”

First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through in the next round, in the manner they’ve done it, the atmosphere they have created, and, yeah, a really sad day for us.

I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players. I haven’t seen anyone not doing what is required at this level. But, obviously, we insisted so much, we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, obviously, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. And football is about that.

Attitude wise, absolutely zero [wrong] otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way. It had nothing to do with effort or application or determination to win it, but we lack other things to, to create a much bigger margin than today, with what we produce, they really should have been shown in the scoreline.

Something that we discussed already before the match.

It’s difficult to see on the cameras, I prefer to watch it back properly and I will assess the situation.

We will learn from everything [on if he will learn from it].

I don’t think it will [sink in], it’s really hard to address the players when we have a league game on Saturday and I didn’t want to be the bearer of reality. The biggest night in the club’s history. We’ve beaten the champions, somehow!

We knew before the game, we’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we’re going to go and outplay them. So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.

Obviously, the goal happens, but they’re going to happen; they’re so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.

To beat the English champions on penalties, credit to everyone one of these lads. We looked at Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We compared it even though these are the champions. We thought ‘if we lay it all out there, let’s see what happens.

The team who are 18th in League Two have beaten the Premier League champions. Nine perfect penalties and one miss from Bruno Guimaraes.

Lynch dives to his left after the Guimaraes stutter, good save from the goalkeeper.

Arsenal are out if Haughey converts this penalty.

Cannon scores against Arsenal at Highbury. Bruno G up next.

Gyokeres finishes with power. The perfect record continues. Cannon up next for Fleetwood.

Meslier dives the wrong way again, Davies does well to keep his composure after needing a few attempts to spot the ball.

All four penalties have been scored, Havertz sends Lynch the wrong way after missing a few chances in regulation time.

Cracking penalty from midfielder, into the roof of the net with power.

Lynch guessed the right way, but Odegaard found the bottom-right corner with power.

He waits for Meslier to dive and rolls the ball into the opposite corner.

Odegaard is going to take first for Arsenal.

Their striker Coughlan, on as a sub in the second half, is going to take the first penalty of the shoot-out against Meslier.

Arsenal taken to penalties by the team 18th in League Two. They finish the game with a sense of injustice after Max Dowman’s red card, but they only have themselves to blame for not putting Fleetwood to the sword in the second half. Huge defensive effort from the underdogs.

Arsenal continue to pile the pressure on even with 10 men, but Guimaraes’s cross is claimed by Lynch.

Fleetwood then go on the attack, and White makes a mess of Rooney’s cross, conceding a cheap corner.

One last chance to win the tie, but Arsenal deal with it.

Havertz then heads the ball down in a dangerous zone but no Arsenal player is there. Arsenal have had their best spell since the red card, almost playing with some anger.

Brilliant save from Lynch to deny Ben White at the back post! Stopped right on the line, just as five minutes of stoppage time are shown on the board.

Then Lynch turns behind another Odegaard shot for a corner.

HUGE save from Jay Lynch! https://t.co/dLJaFwCmHQ

Bruno Guimaraes floats in a cross that is too heavy for Ben White. Fleetwood have a free-kick which they are going to send into the mixer but Arsenal clear.

Mikel Arteta did not have much sympathy for Dowman as he walked past him, but replays suggest it was a harsh call. No VAR in play tonight. Arsenal now playing with 10 for the final minutes.

I suspect Mikel Arteta will feel a little differently about this situation when he sees a replay of what actually happened. https://t.co/tflU7nc831

The Arsenal winger reacted to a heavy challenge, and the referee has judged that he kicked out. There was very little in the incident, a slight movement of his left leg rather than a full-on swing.

RED CARD for Max Dowman! 🟥 https://t.co/wq4EvRIScm

Fleetwood’s best attacking moment of the second half! White and Mosquera got themselves in a mess before Meslier made a smothering save from Davies. Havertz heads the resulting corner clear but Eze messes up a promising Arsenal break.

Arsenal continue to hog possession around the Fleetwood box, but since both teams made their subs, the home team have started to look more comfortable again. Eze’s shot is blocked, and then he is caught offside.

Arsenal making another couple of changes: Guimaraes and Konsa replace Lewis-Skelly and Zubimendi.

For Fleetwood: Davies replaces Loupalo-Bi.

Ben White caught offside just as Arsenal were building up a head of steam in attack. “Champion of England, you’re having a laugh” is the chant from the home fans.

From that Arsenal free-kick, Havertz’s low cross goes straight into the side-netting. The German has had a bit of a stinker, Arsenal will need better at Anfield on Sunday. I’m sure Arteta would have liked to have taken off Havertz or Gyokeres by now.

Haughey wins an important tackle on Lewis-Skelly after Arsenal found the free player in the box, and from the resulting short corner Dowman’s shot is straight Lynch.

Dowman is then hacked down by Batty, who was tempted in by a heavy touch. Booking for the Fleetwood defender.

If the game finishes level, we will go straight to penalties. One or two players on both teams with heavy legs, but Arsenal surely have to turn the screw from here.

Coughlan is an in-form striker who is trying to offer Fleetwood some more intensity and pressing from the front. Despite all that Arsenal pressure, Fleetwood have not gone under since conceding the equaliser.

Havertz hesitant after Odegaard picked out his run and split the Fleetwood defence again. Neither let fly with the shot from a tight angle, nor picked out a cutback. Two changes from Fleetwood: Evans and McClean off, Coughlan and Murphy on.

And a change from Arsenal: O’Neill off, replaced by Eze. O’Neill was one of Arsenal’s brighter starters.

Bodies on the line from Fleetwood to keep the scores level, first Havertz and then Lewis Skelly had shots blocked from a free-kick floated into the box. Fleetwood need to hope for a second wind from somewhere.

#1180. Tebas lists Real Madrid’s attacks on LaLiga a month after club demanded his resignation

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

Javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas says Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

Earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez said Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

Tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

The thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club said Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

The same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas said the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

The dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid said it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

Pérez now faces his members. Their representatives will gather at Ciudad Real Madrid’s basketball venue for two assemblies called by the board, with remote attendance also possible. The only item at the extraordinary assembly is a proposal to ratify tennis player Rafael Nadal as a board member. The ordinary assembly opens at 9:00 on first call and 10:00 on second call, with Pérez’s report as its opening item.
